# onpager_service_account (Resource)

Manage a native OnPager service account, its management owner and active state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_service_account" "example" {
  display_name = "Configuration automation"
  active       = true
  # Omitted owner_team_id selects tenant-level management.
  # No roles or tokens are created by this resource.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Account label of 1–128 UTF-8 bytes, without NUL or leading/trailing whitespace. Display names need not be unique.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the account is active. Defaults to `true`. Disabling revokes every account key. Reactivation requires an active owner team and never revives revoked keys. Refresh/import preserve inactive accounts without mutations.
- `owner_team_id` (String) Management owner team UUID. Omission or `null` means tenant-level management and clears any prior owner. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set. Updates require `service_accounts.update` in both old and new areas. Ownership does not grant business access or limit the account's roles.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.

## Import

Import using the account UUID, including inactive accounts. A later apply
reconciles metadata and `active` state.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_service_account.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_service_account.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Lifecycle

This resource manages account metadata, management ownership and active state.
Tokens and role assignments are managed separately. Account writes are
unversioned and do not send `If-Match`.

Destroy deactivates the account and atomically revokes all its keys. The UUID,
history and role assignments remain. Already inactive accounts remain inactive.
Failure retains state. Use credentials independent of the account being retired;
reactivation does not restore revoked keys.

Management ownership is independent of role assignments. Disabling an owner team
deactivates its owned accounts and revokes their keys. Transfer ownership before
retiring a team if the account must stay active. Clearing `owner_team_id`
transfers management to tenant scope.

## Permissions

Requires explicit native grants `service_accounts.create`,
`service_accounts.read`, `service_accounts.update`,
`service_accounts.deactivate` and `service_accounts.reactivate` in the stored
management owner's scope. An unowned account requires tenant grants. Owner
changes require update authority in both the old and new scopes. Destroy also
requires read authority to identify an already inactive account. Creating an
account does not grant it configuration access.
